Sniper Elite Resistance is a third person shooter with stealth mechanics, set in France during World War 2, where player character and British soldier Harry Hawker must stop the Nazis from developing a deadly super weapon.

This is the fourth game in the series that I’ve played, having previously played Sniper Elite 3, 4 and 5.

[h1]Gameplay (high quality)[/h1]

•	Each mission takes place on a fairly large map, whose layout allows you to approach objectives from multiple directions. There are lots of buildings to search for supplies, or to use as cover during combat. And each mission contains multiple optional secondary objectives.

•	The player can equip three weapons, a pistol, sub machine gun, and sniper rifle. There are different versions of each weapon to unlock, which can be modified to improve their values for damage, clip size, fire rate, zoom scope, etc.

•	You can also carry various consumables such as medkits, grenades and mines. I like using explosives to set traps on corpses of enemy soldiers, which will detonate when their comrades come closer to investigate.

•	You’re often heavily outnumbered, so using stealth to gain an advantage can be useful, although its tricky to progress completely unseen. Silenced guns still make some noise, and can alert nearby enemies. However, loud background noises such as planes flying overhead, thunder claps, and explosions, can mask your rifle shots if you time them correctly. You can also sneak up behind enemies to get a melee kill.

•	When your presence is detected, this usually leads to a lengthy fight against large numbers of soldiers, especially if they raise an alarm to summon reinforcements.

•	Enemy AI is mostly fine, although they can occasionally do some dumb things. They’ll try to flank you during active combat, and if they don’t know where you are, they’ll search the area around the noise of your last gunshot. But like any stealth game, if you’re able to hide for long enough, they’ll assume that everything is fine now and reset to normal patrol patterns.

[h1]Story (low quality)[/h1]

•	Story is quite generic and basically the same as previous games. The Nazis are developing another super weapon and you are the lone soldier behind enemy lines trying to stop it, with occasional intel provided by local resistance.

•	The new player character makes no difference to the story. You could literally cut and paste Karl Fairburne into this game and the only thing that would change is his accent.

•	Voice acting is average.

•	This is a new story which doesn’t connect to the previous games, so you won’t feel confused if this is your first time playing Sniper Elite.

[h1]Technical (medium quality)[/h1]

•	It took me 14 hours to complete the campaign and the four DLC missions. There’s also a survival mode where you need to defend control points against massive waves of enemy soldiers, which could provide a few more hours of entertainment.

•	I had no problems with framerate, stuttering, bugs or crashes. (RTX 3080, i7-12700K, 32GB DDR4, 1440p).

•	Quality of anti-aliasing is terrible. There’s frequently visible shimmering or flickering on the edges of buildings, fences, trees, and other objects. This seems to be a common problem for this developer / game engine.

•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.

[h1]Recommendation[/h1]

Sniper Elite Resistance is a good game, which fans of third person shooters should enjoy. Combat and story are both very similar to previous games, so if you’re a fan of the series, this one is worth playing, although its probably best to wait for a sale. If you’re new to Sniper Elite, I’d suggest picking up 4 and 5 on a sale too.
